dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. What can I do for you tonight?
Hi, Denise. Can I get your last name, please? I'm writing everything down this time.
Sure, it's Arruda. A-R-R-U-D-A.

A-R-R-U-D-A. Okay. My name's Diogo Resendes, I'm calling about my parents' house, 14 Wellington Avenue, Fifth Ward. The basement flooded again. Last night, overnight Sunday into today. That's the second time this winter.
Oh no. Okay, 14 Wellington. Was there an earlier report on this?

Yes. My father, Carlos Resendes, called on Monday the twelfth, after the storm on the tenth. That one was about six inches. He talked to a Lorraine, she said a crew would check the corner drain on Wednesday the fourteenth. And a crew did come, I'll give them that. They cleared off the grate and shoveled the silt out around the top of the basin. That's it. Nobody looked at the line. And now here we are, two weeks later, same thing.
I've got your father's call here, and the visit on the fourteenth. Grate and basin top cleaned. Okay. Tell me about last night.

About four inches this time. Same two spots as before, exactly the same. The floor drain backs up, and water comes through the window well glass on the street side. Nothing new. Because the drain at the corner backs up and the street fills, and it's just got nowhere to go but in.
Same entry points, about four inches. And what got wet?

The spare refrigerator and the holiday decorations. Again. We'd just dried that stuff out. Nothing else this time, but honestly that's luck. And it's not just us. The next two houses had water in their cellars too. I talked to both of them this morning.
Okay, I'm noting the two neighboring houses as well. That's helpful.
I've also got a photo log. Dates on everything. The first flood, the grate after the crew left, the street last night, the basement this morning. If somebody wants it, I'll send it.
Good, hang onto that. Whoever comes out will want to see it.

See, that's my point, though. I don't want another crew to come rake off the grate and leave. With respect. Clearing the top obviously didn't fix anything. I want a supervisor or an engineer to actually look at that drain. Something's wrong under there.

Understood. Here's what I'm doing. I'm logging this as a repeat backup, not a new one, so it's tied to your father's report. I'm booking a crew for Wednesday, the twenty-eighth, and I'm putting a note on it that the grate was already cleared and the problem came back, so they need to look at the line itself.
Wednesday the twenty-eighth. Line, not grate. Okay. And the supervisor?
I'm requesting a supervisor callback, and that should happen by Thursday the twenty-ninth. What's the best number for that?
My cell. 401-555-0186. Please call me, not the house. My father gets nervous on the phone with this stuff.
401-555-0186, Diogo. Got it. If the crew finds something on Wednesday, the supervisor will have that when they call you.
[pause] Sorry, I'm writing. Repeat backup, crew Wednesday the twenty-eighth, supervisor call by Thursday the twenty-ninth. Is there a reference number?
It's filed under the address, so anybody here who pulls up 14 Wellington will see both floods and both calls. Just give them the address and say it's the repeat backup.

Okay. Look, I know you're not the one who decided to just clean the grate. But I spent my day off in a wet basement, and right now I'm standing in my parents' kitchen eating leftover Christmas ham out of a container because nobody had time to cook. I really don't want to be calling a third time.
I hear you. I put it in strong. Wednesday they're there to look underneath, and the supervisor's on it after that.
Alright. Thank you, Denise. I'll be watching for Wednesday.
You do that. Get some rest tonight, okay?
